change.title: Content update: rule 0291 for template T7

verdict.headline: Change w-y6p3/change/0291 breaks: rule-0291 rejected by rule-validator with message "fields ['f21'] beyond 20"
verdict.cause: The change adds rule-0291 with criteria on f02 and f21 for template T7. The dependency chain: change → rule-0291 interface → template:T7 (matches_on=f02,f21) → content-pipeline → rule-validator.validate. The rule-validator (ic-0045) checks the rule against template:T7's field_count=21. The rule-validator also enforces a inputs_supplied=20 constraint (ic-0051). Rule-0291 references field f21, which exceeds the 20-field limit enforced by the validator, causing rejection. Baseline experiment x-41215c45e02445e7 had 0 rejections; candidate experiment x-b62718f0eebc4918 rejected 1 rule with message "rule-0291: rejected, fields ['f21'] beyond 20". The rejected rule was held back by validation, so only 3 of 4 rules were shipped to the interpreter (exit_code=0, matches=0).
tested: x-41215c45e02445e7: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-b62718f0eebc4918: candidate · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations: The investigator predicted a failure, but the experiments showed none under the tested conditions; read its explanation with caution.
The exact source of the "20" limit in the rejection message was not independently verified - it could be the validator's internal constraint
or the template's field_count=21 (ic-0044). No test was run to isolate which specific contract triggered the rejection.
Baseline and candidate both passed under every tested workload.

causal_chain.edge: h1: rule-validator.validate (ic-0045) checks the rule's field references against its internal limit. The validator has a 20-field threshold; rule-0291 references f21, surpassing this limit and causing rejection. Template T7's field_count=21 (ic-0044) is the declared contract, but the validator enforces a stricter 20-limit.

hypotheses.claim: Rule-0291 fails the rule-validator's field count check and is rejected from the pipeline because it references field f21, which exceeds the validator's internal limit of 20 fields, even though template T7 has field_count=21
hypotheses.mechanism: rule-validator.validate (ic-0045) checks the rule's field references against its internal limit. The validator has a 20-field threshold; rule-0291 references f21, surpassing this limit and causing rejection. Template T7's field_count=21 (ic-0044) is the declared contract, but the validator enforces a stricter 20-limit.

hypotheses.claim: Content-interpreter will fail to evaluate rule-0291 because it expects inputs_supplied=20 (ic-0046) but rule-0291 only defines criteria for 2 fields (f02, f21), causing a mismatch in the number of inputs the interpreter can process
hypotheses.mechanism: content-interpreter.load_rules (ic-0046) expects inputs_supplied=20 when evaluating template T7. The rule-0291 only specifies criteria for 2 fields. After the rule passes the rule-validator (if it does), the interpreter will encounter a mismatch between the expected 20 inputs and the 2 criteria fields provided, causing evaluation failure.

issues.statement: The rule-validator (ic-0045) enforces an internal field count limit of 20 (despite template T7's declared field_count=21 in ic-0044).
issues.problem: contradicted: ic-0045 says rule-validator.validate checks against template:T7 with contract_key=field_count, contract_value=21. ic-0051 says rule-validator.validate checks against content-interpreter.load_rules with contract_key=inputs_supplied, contract_value=20. ic-0046 says content-interpreter.load_rules evaluates template:T7 with contract_key=inputs_supplied, contract_value=20. So the validator checks against template's field_count=21, but the interpreter only accepts inputs_supplied=20. The validator's internal limit is not explicitly stated as 20; it's the interpreter that has a 20-field limit. The explanation misattributes the 20-field limit to the validator.
